style.vernacular: Low-rise coastal capital held to a white/cream palette by long-standing planning custom: 1-4 storey flat-roofed villas and apartment blocks in white or sand painted render, pointed and trefoil arches, crenellated parapets and carved wooden doors, with Omani forts and watchtowers on the bare brown volcanic hills; new civic buildings use pale sandstone or limestone with Omani-Islamic arches and domes; the ground is sand and gravel with palms and ghaf/acacia in planted verges.
style.ornament: Omani pointed and trefoil arches, merlon-style crenellated parapets (forts and watchtowers), carved teak doors with brass studs, geometric screens and mashrabiya-style lattices, gilded dome finials, khanjar and frankincense-burner motifs on civic furniture.

sources.what: low-lying white buildings typical of Muscat; forts (Al Jalali, Al Mirani); hot desert climate, sparse sabkha vegetation, bare hills
Indian sandstone Omani-Islamic civic architecture with five minarets and central dome
Zawawi Mosque: golden-coloured single dome and minaret, Quran engraved on metal wall panels, wood and marble
